faq.a: Konul is associated with the Turkic form قُونُول, whose core sense is konul; heart, soul (turkic).

faq.q: What is the origin of Konul?
faq.a: Konul is associated with Turkic. Konul is a Turkic (Azerbaijani) female given name, from könül ('heart, soul').
No — the underlying form is Turkic, not Arabic.
Konul can occur in Muslim naming contexts, but it is better described as a Turkic-origin name used within some Muslim naming traditions than as an exclusively Islamic religious term.
Konul should not be classified as a Quranic personal name without a direct Quranic basis. Könül is a Turkic word, not a Quranic Arabic form.

faq.a: Romanization variants include Konul, konul. Script forms are قونول, قُونُول, क़ोनुल.

faq.q: Is Konul a boy's or girl's name?
faq.a: Documented usage records this form as female. Gender is not inferred from the meaning of the word, and actual use may vary between communities.
